{{Short description|German astronomer}}
[[File:Frank-eisenhauer.jpg|thumb|Frank Eisenhauer]]
'''Frank Eisenhauer''' (born 9 June 1968 in [[Augsburg]]) is a German [[astronomer]] and [[astrophysicist]], scientific member of the [[Max Planck Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eisenhauer, Frank |url=https://www.mpg.de/20379632/extraterrestrial-physics-eisenhauer |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=www.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics]] (MPE),<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpe.mpg.de/7948075/news20230515|title=Frank Eisenhauer becomes new director at the MPI for Extraterrestrial Physics|website=www.mpe.mpg.de}}</ref> and a professor at the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM). He is best known for his contributions to interferometry and spectroscopy and the study of the [[black hole]] at the centre of the [[Milky Way]].

== Life ==
Eisenhauer grew up in Augsburg. In 1987, he graduated from the Justus-von-Liebig Gymnasium in [[Neusäß]] and then did his military service with the Mountain Signal Battalion 8 in [[Murnau am Staffelsee|Murnau]]. Eisenhauer is widowed, has three children and lives in [[Munich]].
== Studies ==
Eisenhauer studied physics at the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM) (1988–1995) and has been working at the [[Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics]] (MPE) since his diploma thesis in 1995. There, he wrote his doctoral thesis under later Nobel Laureate [[Reinhard Genzel]] and received his doctorate from [[LMU Munich]] in 1998. In 2011, Eisenhauer habilitated at TUM.

== Teaching ==
Eisenhauer is adjunct professor and TUM distinguished affiliated professor<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-10 |title=TUM Distinguished Affiliated Professorships Awards 2025 |url=https://www.nat.tum.de/en/nat/latest/physics/article/tum-distinguished-affiliated-professorships-awards-2025/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=www.nat.tum.de |language=en}}</ref> at TUM, where he teaches astrophysics and high-resolution astronomy.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://campus.tum.de/tumonline/visitenkarte.show_vcard?pPersonenGruppe=3&pPersonenId=DB021172F366B24F | title=Visitenkarte von Eisenhauer, Frank; Apl. Prof. Dr. Rer. Nat. Habil. – TUMonline – Technische Universität München }}</ref>

== Science and research ==
As a director of the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE), Eisenhauer leads the development and scientific evaluation of large astronomical instruments. Eisenhauer has been instrumental in the development of astronomy with the highest spatial resolution and imaging spectroscopy, contributing in particular to the discovery and study of the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.<ref name="g679">{{cite journal | last1=Genzel | first1=Reinhard | last2=Eisenhauer | first2=Frank | last3=Gillessen | first3=Stefan | title=The Galactic Center massive black hole and nuclear star cluster | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | volume=82 | issue=4 | date=20 December 2010 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.82.3121 | doi-access=free | pages=3121–3195 | arxiv=1006.0064 | bibcode=2010RvMP...82.3121G }}</ref>

Already in his doctoral thesis, Eisenhauer worked on [[infrared astronomy]] and developed an infrared camera with [[Fabry-Pérot]] spectrometer for the adaptive optics at the 3.6m telescope of the [[European Southern Observatory]] (ESO) in [[La Silla Observatory|La Silla]] (Chile). Subsequently, as Principal Investigator, he led the development of the SPIFFI/SINFONI spectrometer at the ESO [[Very Large Telescope]] in Paranal (Chile), which, with a then unique combination of adaptive optics and imaging spectroscopy,<ref name="h510">{{cite journal | last1=Eisenhauer | first1=Frank | last2=Raab | first2=Walfried | title=Visible/Infrared Imaging Spectroscopy and Energy-Resolving Detectors | journal=Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics | volume=53 | issue=1 | date=18 August 2015 | issn=0066-4146 | doi=10.1146/annurev-astro-082214-122442 | doi-access=free | pages=155–197 | bibcode=2015ARA&A..53..155E }}</ref> not only corrects for the interference caused by the Earth's atmosphere, but also simultaneously records a spectrum for each pixel in the image. In 2003, this enabled Eisenhauer and colleagues to measure the distance to the centre of the Milky Way from the orbit of the star S2 for the first time using geometric methods,<ref name="j115">{{cite journal | last1=Eisenhauer | first1=F. | last2=Schdel | first2=R. | last3=Genzel | first3=R. | last4=Ott | first4=T. | last5=Tecza | first5=M. | last6=Abuter | first6=R. | last7=Eckart | first7=A. | last8=Alexander | first8=T. | title=A Geometric Determination of the Distance to the Galactic Center | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | volume=597 | issue=2 | date=10 November 2003 | issn=0004-637X | doi=10.1086/380188 | doi-access=free | pages=L121–L124 | arxiv=astro-ph/0306220 | bibcode=2003ApJ...597L.121E }}</ref> and by measuring the radial velocities of several stars, they were able to confirm the assumption that a supermassive black hole is located there.<ref name="a208">{{cite journal | last1=Eisenhauer | first1=F. | last2=Genzel | first2=R. | last3=Alexander | first3=T. | last4=Abuter | first4=R. | last5=Paumard | first5=T. | last6=Ott | first6=T. | last7=Gilbert | first7=A. | last8=Gillessen | first8=S. | last9=Horrobin | first9=M. | last10=Trippe | first10=S. | last11=Bonnet | first11=H. | last12=Dumas | first12=C. | last13=Hubin | first13=N. | last14=Kaufer | first14=A. | last15=Kissler-Patig | first15=M. | last16=Monnet | first16=G. | last17=Strobele | first17=S. | last18=Szeifert | first18=T. | last19=Eckart | first19=A. | last20=Schodel | first20=R. | last21=Zucker | first21=S. |display-authors=3 | title=SINFONI in the Galactic Center: Young Stars and Infrared Flares in the Central Light-Month | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | volume=628 | issue=1 | date=20 July 2005 | issn=0004-637X | doi=10.1086/430667 | doi-access=free | pages=246–259 | arxiv=astro-ph/0502129 | bibcode=2005ApJ...628..246E }}</ref>

P. |last11=Beust |first11=H. |last12=Blind |first12=N. |last13=Bonnefoy |first13=M. |last14=Bonnet |first14=H. |last15=Bourget |first15=P. |date=2019-03-01 |title=First direct detection of an exoplanet by optical interferometry - Astrometry and K-band spectroscopy of HR 8799 e |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/abs/2019/03/aa35253-19/aa35253-19.html |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |language=en |volume=623 |pages=L11 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201935253 |arxiv=1903.11903 |bibcode=2019A&A...623L..11G |hdl=1887/85083 |issn=0004-6361}}</ref> and first resolution of microlensed images.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dong |first1=Subo |last2=Mérand |first2=A. |last3=Delplancke-Ströbele |first3=F. |last4=Gould |first4=Andrew |last5=Chen |first5=Ping |last6=Post |first6=R. |last7=Kochanek |first7=C. L. |last14=Shappee |first14=B. J. |last15=Thompson |first15=Todd A. |date=2019-01-20 |title=First Resolution of Microlensed Images* |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=871 |issue=1 |pages=70 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/aaeffb |arxiv=1809.08243 |bibcode=2019ApJ...871...70D |doi-access=free |issn=0004-637X}}</ref>

The SINFONI and GRAVITY instruments are part of the instrument suite employed in the discovery and characterization of the Galactic Center Black Hole, for which [[Reinhard Genzel]] and [[Andrea Ghez]] have been awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2020/summary/|title = The Nobel Prize in Physics 2020}}</ref>

Since 2020, Eisenhauer is also principal investigator of GRAVITYPlus to upgrade the VLT Interferometer with wide-field fringe tracking and laser guide star adaptive optics. The wide field mode has been implemented in the period 2019-2022,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abuter |first1=R. |last2=Allouche |first2=F. |last3=Amorim |first3=A. |last4=Bailet |first4=C. |last5=Bauböck |first5=M. |last6=Berger |first6=J.-P. |last7=Berio |first7=P. |last8=Bigioli |first8=A. |last9=Boebion |first9=O. |last10=Bolzer |first10=M. L. |last11=Bonnet |first11=H. |last12=Bourdarot |first12=G. |last13=Bourget |first13=P. |last14=Brandner |first14=W. |last15=Clénet |first15=Y. |date=2022-09-01 |title=First light for GRAVITY Wide - Large separation fringe tracking for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/abs/2022/09/aa43941-22/aa43941-22.html |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |language=en |volume=665 |pages=A75 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/202243941 |arxiv=2206.00684 |bibcode=2022A&A...665A..75G |hdl=1887/3561319 |issn=0004-6361}}</ref> the new adaptive optics in 2024.<ref>{{Citation |last=Collaboration |first=GRAVITY+ |title=First Light for the GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics: Extreme Adaptive Optics for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer |date=2025-09-25 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21431 |access-date=2025-10-06 |arxiv=2509.21431 }}</ref> The laser guide stars will be available starting 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESO - GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics with Laser Guide Stars Science Verification on VLTI-UT |url=https://www.eso.org/sci/publications/announcements/sciann17716.html |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=www.eso.org}}</ref> 

The MPE IR/Submm department of Frank Eisenhauer and Reinhard Genzel also leads the development of [[MICADO]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=information@eso.org |title=MICADO {{!}} ELT {{!}} ESO |url=https://elt.eso.org/instrument/MICADO/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=elt.eso.org |language=en}}</ref> a first-light camera and spectrograph for the European [[Extremely Large Telescope]] (ELT).<ref>{{Cite web |last=information@eso.org |title=ELT {{!}} ESO |url=https://elt.eso.org/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=elt.eso.org |language=en}}</ref> 

Other areas of research to which Eisenhauer's observations have contributed include galaxy dynamics in the [[early universe]],<ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006Natur.442..786G The rapid formation of a large rotating disk galaxy three billion years after the Big Bang] Genzel, R., [[Linda Tacconi|Tacconi, L. J.]], Eisenhauer, F., et al. 2006: "The rapid formation of a large rotating disk galaxy three billion years after the Big Bang", Nature, 442, 786</ref> [[active galactic nuclei]], and [[star formation]] in massive [[star clusters]].<ref name="t446">{{cite journal | author=GRAVITY Collaboration | title=Spatially resolved rotation of the broad-line region of a quasar at sub-parsec scale | journal=Nature | volume=563 | issue=7733 | date=2018 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/s41586-018-0731-9 | doi-access=free | pages=657–660 | pmid=30487613 | arxiv=1811.11195 | bibcode=2018Natur.563..657G | url=https://hal.sorbonne-universite.fr/hal-01953271/document | access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* TUM Distinguished Affiliated Professor of the [[Technical University of Munich]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Eisenhauer appointed as honorary professor at TU Munich |url=https://www.mpe.mpg.de/8053359/news20250221 |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=www.mpe.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>
* Instrument Development Award 2023 by [[Astronomische Gesellschaft]] for development of SINFONI and GRAVITY Instruments<ref name="k484">{{cite web |date=6 December 2021 |title=Outstanding Research Awarded by the German Astronomical Society |url=https://astronomische-gesellschaft.de/en/News/outstanding-research-awarded-by-the-german-astronomical-society?set_language=en |access-date=18 February 2025 |website=Plone site}}</ref>
* [[Gruber Prize in Cosmology]] 2022 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gruber.yale.edu/cosmology|title=Cosmology &#124; Gruber Foundation|website=gruber.yale.edu}}</ref> for designing instruments that collected evidence for a black hole at the center of our galaxy
* [[Stern–Gerlach Medal]] 2022 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/stern-gerlach-medaille/preistraeger|title=Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger|website=DPG}}</ref> of the [[German Physical Society]] for the pioneering work in high-resolution infrared astronomy
* [[Jackson-Gwilt Medal]] 2022 from the [[Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref>[https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/RAS%20Jackson%20Gwilt%20Medal%20-%20Dr%20Frank%20Eisenhauer%20(1).pdf Eisenhauer]</ref> for the development of astronomical instrumentation
* Foreign associate to the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2021<ref name="v440">{{cite web |date=1 December 2021 |title=Frank Eisenhauer |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/frank-eisenhauer |access-date=18 February 2025 |website=Académie des sciences |language=fr}}</ref>
* [[Tycho Brahe Medal]] 2021 from the [[European Astronomical Society]]<ref>[https://eas.unige.ch/documents/eas_prizes_2021.pdf EAS Prizes]</ref> for the leadership of the SINFONI and  GRAVITY instruments
* Michelson Investigator Achievement Award 2020 for the groundbreaking results of VLTI-GRAVITY<ref name="s276">{{cite web | title=Frank Eisenhauer receives 2020 Michelson Investigator Achievement Award | website=mpe.mpg.de | date=25 October 2023 | url=https://www.mpe.mpg.de/7897616/news20220722 | access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref>
